name: Exact
works_with: Web, macOS, iOS and Linux apps. Built on a Mac with Xcode; Linux works for the web loop and the Linux host
short: Write one app in a small UI language plus TypeScript or Rust, and it runs natively on the web, macOS, iOS and Linux.
what: Exact is a cross-platform app runtime from Expo. You describe the interface in Contract, a small declarative language, and write the data logic in TypeScript or Rust. Each platform draws with its own tools, with no webview, and a coding agent can build, run, screenshot and test the app on every host through one script.
who: Developers who want one codebase for native desktop, mobile and web apps and are happy to work from a fast-changing source checkout. Skip it if you need a stable API today: the project is pre-1.0 and says so.
needs: Bun 1.4.2, the version the project pins. Node and npm are not needed
Google Chrome, which the agent uses to drive the web host
Xcode 27.1 or later for the macOS and iOS hosts
Hermes only for TypeScript apps on native hosts. The setup script installs the pinned bundle

steps.title: Install the pinned Bun
steps.text: This puts Bun 1.4.2 beside any Bun you already have. Use `~/.bun-1.4.2/bin/bun` if it is not on your PATH.

steps.title: Clone it and run the Caltrain demo in the browser
steps.text: The first run compiles the toolchain and takes a few minutes. Then edit `apps/caltrain/app.contract` and the page reloads in about a tenth of a second.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/expo/exact.git
cd exact
bun scripts/exact.mjs setup
bun host/web/dev.mjs            # Caltrain, at http://127.0.0.1:8765/

steps.title: Run it natively
steps.text: A first native build takes ten to fifteen minutes on a laptop. Later builds take a minute or two.
steps.code:
bun host/apple/build.mjs --run              # macOS
bun host/apple/build.mjs --ios --run        # an iOS Simulator (--device --run for a connected iPhone)
cargo build --profile host-dev -p caltrain-linux   # Linux: a DRM/KMS console, or headless anywhere (--release to ship)

steps.title: Drive it the way an agent does
steps.text: Swap `web` for `macos`, `ios` or `linux` once that host is built.
steps.code:
bun host/web/build.mjs caltrain-web         # the build the agent's web host serves
bun scripts/agent.mjs web tree "tap change-station" "type station-search Palo" state "screenshot out.png"
bun scripts/agent.mjs web --test apps/caltrain/app.test.contract

steps.title: Make your own app
steps.text: `exact new` creates `app.contract` for the view, `app.ts` for the data and an `AGENTS.md` that points your agent at the one guide it must read.
steps.code:
bun scripts/exact.mjs new ../hello          # or run `bun link` once, then `exact new ../hello`
cd ../hello
bun exact.mjs contract types app.contract -o app.contract.d.ts   # first run builds the compiler
bun exact.mjs web                           # the dev loop, at http://127.0.0.1:8765/
bun exact.mjs test web tests/*.test.contract # the app's *.test.contract, or the files named
bun exact.mjs mac --run                     # this Mac
bun exact.mjs ios --run                     # an iOS Simulator

try.label: From the README
try.text: Clone https://github.com/expo/exact and follow its README to make a new Exact app with `exact new`. Run `bun scripts/exact.mjs setup` once first. Make a todo list where I can add items, check them off, delete them, and see how many are left. Put the view in Contract and keep the list in `app.ts`. Write an `app.test.contract`, pass it on web, macOS, and the iOS Simulator with `scripts/agent.mjs`, then open the app for me on all three.

watch: Exact is pre-1.0 and changes daily, with no API stability, no backwards compatibility and no migration guide.
There is no packaged CLI. You work from a source checkout, and new apps refer to it by path.
The Bun install command pipes a script from bun.sh straight into bash. Read the script first.

An app's `AGENTS.md` asks your agent to record friction notes. They go to Expo only if you allow it (the default asks first). `bun exact.mjs feedback never` turns it off for a project, and `EXACT_FEEDBACK=0` blocks every send on the machine.
The README's sample agent run took about 57 minutes, about 25 of them on the first macOS and iOS builds.
Windows and Android are early. Text editing works on the web and Apple hosts, and Linux only reads.
